Montana has introduced no AI legislation as of September 2026, making it one of the states that has not yet entered the policy record on this subject.

The absence of bills means there is no state-level legal friction, and no state-level legal protection, for AI deployment within Montana's borders. That cuts both ways: infrastructure builders face no Montana-specific compliance layer, but operators also cannot point to any Montana statute governing data use, automated decision-making, or algorithmic accountability.

The data covers only formal legislative activity. It says nothing about executive orders, agency rulemaking, local ordinances, or federal rules that apply in Montana. A zero count reflects the legislature's output, not the full regulatory environment a data center developer or AI operator would actually face.
